 Order
Heard finally with the consent of both the parties.

1. This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 11.08.2018 passed by IVth Additional Member, MACT Mandsaur in MACC No. 61/2017 whereby an award of Rs. 4,26,400/- has been passed in favor of Respondent No. 1 to 4 regarding death of Mangibai in motor vehicle accident.

2. Facts in brief are that, the mother of Respondent No. 2 to 4 and wife of Respondent No. 1 Smt.
Mangibai was coming after treatment from Bhanpura to Dhamaniya Fante on 08.07.2016.
At about 8:30 PM, she arrived at from the bus at Dhamaniya Fante and was proceeded to Dhamniya.

Respondent No. 5 hit the Mangibai while driving the Mahendra Bolero bearing Registration No.
MP-03-A2431 by rash and negligent driving at Dhamniya Fante.
Mangibai sustained grievous injury and succumbed to injuries.
The vehicle No. MP-03- A2431 was also damaged totally.

The vehicle No.
MP-03-A2431 driven by Respondent No. 5 under the ownership and control of appellants.
A claim of Rs. 23,71,500/- was preferred submitting that the age of the deceased Mangibai was 51 years and she was earning Rs. 19,000/- pm by homework and working as a laborer.

Appellants and Respondent No. 5did not file any reply and the proceedings were proceeded against them ex parte.
3.

The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the testimony of Mangilal as [PW-1], Bhuwani Shankar as [PW-2] and admitted the documents [Ex. P-1] to [P-14] that are the certified copies of record of Criminal Case No. 1299/2016 from the file of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sitamau District Mandsaur.
3 . Appreciating the evidence Tribunal assessed the age of deceased Mangibai as 58 years, her per month income is Rs. 4500/- and also concluded that the Mangibai died due to rash and negligent driving of Mahendra Bolero Vehicle No. MP-03-A2431 driven by Respondent No. 5 and allowed 10 % enhancement in the head of future prospect, deducted the 1/3rd for personnel expenses of Mangibai and applying the multiplier of 9 calculated the total loss of dependency Rs. 3,56,400/-,
allowed Rs. 15,000/- in the head of funeral expenses, Rs. 15,000/- in the head of loss of estate and Rs. 40,000/- in the head of loss of consortium and held liable appellants and respondent No. 5 to pay the awarded amount jointly and severally with interest of 6% pa from the date of application i.e.,
02.01.2017.

sentences.text: Challenging the award this appeal has been preferred on the ground that Tribunal has committed mistake in holding the negligence of Respondent No. 5 as the deceased was herself negligent.
The income of the deceased has been assessed on higher side & instead of 8, the multiplier of 9 has been applied.
An amount in the head of funeral expenses has been awarded twicely.
The amount on loss of consortium has been wrongly awarded.
The concerned Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation if Respondent No.1 to 4 are found to be eligible.

5. Respondent No. 1 to 4 has opposed the prayer and submitted that no insurance policy has been disclosed and they did not contest the case before the Tribunal and multiplier has been applied properly.
The amount in the head of consortium has not been awarded to the children of Mangibai i.e., Respondent No. 2 to 4, further amount of 1,20,000/- requires to be enhanced.

6. Heard and perused the record.
7.

As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017(4) MACD-1375 (S.C) the multiplier of 9 for the age of 58 years has been properly applied, 10%
enhancement for future prospect is also proper, income of Rs. 4500/- on the date of 08.07.2016 also does not call for interference.

sentences.text: The amount of personnel expenses has been properly deducted.
There is no duplication in the conventional heads.
Even the amount of loss of consortium has not been awarded to respondent No. 2 to 4.
This appeal is totally devoid of merits and is hereby dismissed.
8. The appellants shall bear cost and they have to pay Rs. 10,000/- as a cost of this appeal to Respondent No. 1 to 4.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE Vatan Director General Of Police vs Mangilal on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122620347/
